propositions.text: The principal claimant, his wife, and three sons seek refugee protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (the principal claimant), his wife, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and their three sons, XXXX, XXXX and XXXX XXXX, all citizens of the Czech Republic, with the exception of XXXX, who is a permanent resident of the Czech Republic but also a citizen of Poland, are seeking refugee protection pursuant to ss. 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. (IRPA)

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant, his wife, and three sons seek refugee protection under IRPA, says the court.

propositions.text: The principal claimant's wife was appointed designated representative for her minor son by the Board.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant's wife was appointed by the Board to act as the designated representative on behalf of her minor son, Sebastian.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant's wife was appointed designated representative for her minor son by the Board, says the court.

propositions.text: The principal claimant is ethnically Roma and has faced discrimination and threats from citizens, police, and racist groups since 1989.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant was born in what is now Slovakia. He is ethnically Roma and has experienced discrimination and threats to himself and his family due to his ethnicity. This discrimination, according to the principal claimant, has been at the hands of other citizens, the police and authorities, as well as from overtly racist groups of Neo-Nazis and skinheads who have become more prevalent since the fall of the Communist regime in 1989.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant alleges he is Roma and has faced discrimination and threats from citizens, police, and racist groups since 1989.

propositions.text: The principal claimant alleges police extorted money from him and were defensive when he reported it.
propositions.quote: According to the principal claimant, on one occasion his car was stopped and the police took money from his wallet. When the principal claimant learned of this incident, he took his son to the police station. However, when he told the story and got to the part that it was the police who were the perpetrators, they became very defensive. Reluctantly, they took a report.

propositions.text: Police investigated the incident but did not find the perpetrator; the claimant still had to pay a fine.
propositions.quote: According to the police they investigated the incident and did not find the person who took his money and punched him, however, he still had to pay a fine.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges police extorted money and were defensive; police say they investigated but found no perpetrator and fined claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant's sons faced ethnic abuse in soccer, leading them to leave the team.
propositions.quote: Both of the principal claimant's sons played soccer at a professional level. According to the principal claimant, when he and his wife went to watch the games, the players made fun of their sons for being gypsies. As well as his colleagues disrespecting them, scouts for national teams now ignored them. Finally, the boys left the team as they realized the abuse would not stop.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges his sons faced ethnic abuse in soccer and left the team due to ongoing abuse.

propositions.text: The claimant's wife was accused of stealing at work and physically attacked by a colleague.
propositions.quote: In terms of the principal claimant's wife and her workplace, there had been stealing in the restaurant and the employees were told that the tips would go into a fund to pay for the missing items. Finally, the employees accused the woman married to a "gypsy man of being the only one who would steal." This accusation angered the principal claimant's wife who had been with the restaurant prior to the two other women. An argument ensued and one of the women grabbed her by the hair and shook her.

propositions.text: The claimant advised his wife to leave the restaurant after the attack.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant as a consequence advised his wife to leave the restaurant as he was angry that she had been subjected to this attack.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges his wife was accused of stealing and attacked at work; he advised her to leave the restaurant.

propositions.text: In 2005, the claimant was attacked by four skinheads and made a police report.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2005, the principal claimant had just finished his shift as a cook. As he was walking to his car, he was approached by four young men dressed like skin heads. An unprovoked attack ensued where the claimant was punched and kicked. The principal claimant was bleeding and did not want his wife to see the injuries. He, therefore, went to his parents' house and pretended to be away for a few weeks. The principal claimant made a denunciation to the police.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he was attacked by skinheads in 2005 and reported it to police.

propositions.text: The area where claimants lived had neo-Nazi followers and some clubs banned or harassed gypsies.
propositions.quote: The area where the claimants lived became very popular with neo-Nazi/skinhead followers. Out of the eight restaurants and clubs in the area, four outright banned gypsies from entering. Even in the other clubs, although permitted to enter, they would be harassed by neo-Nazi customers who had been contacted specifically to harass them.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges their area had neo-Nazi followers and clubs banned or harassed gypsies.

propositions.text: In 2008, the claimant's apartment was vandalized with racist graffiti including a swastika.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2008 the principal claimant was leaving his apartment with his two sons. His apartment was vandalized with the words "death to Hungarians" which is how they refer to gypsies in the Czech Republic. There was also a Swastika drawn on the door.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges his apartment was vandalized with racist graffiti and a swastika in 2008.

propositions.text: The claimants arrived in Canada in 2008 and filed claims on June 16, 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimants arrived in Canada on XXXX, 2008 and filed claims on June 16, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The claimants arrived in Canada in 2008 and filed refugee claims on June 16, 2008, says the court.

propositions.text: The Board finds the claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The Board finds that the claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The Board finds the claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection, says the court.

propositions.text: The principal claimant is a Czech citizen; his wife is a Czech permanent resident and Polish citizen; children are Czech citizens, per passports.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant is a citizen of the Czech Republic, his wife is a permanent resident of the Czech Republic but also a citizen of Poland, and the children are citizens of the Czech Republic, as per the certified true copies of their passports.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the claimants' citizenship and residency status per passports.

propositions.text: The determinative issue is state protection.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue is state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the determinative issue is state protection.

propositions.text: There is a presumption that the state can protect citizens unless the state is in complete breakdown.
propositions.quote: There is a presumption, except in situations where the state is in a complete breakdown, that it is capable of protecting its citizens.

propositions.text: Claimants must provide clear and convincing evidence of state's inability to protect to rebut presumption.
propositions.quote: A claimant can rebut this presumption by providing clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect.

propositions.text: Claimants must approach the state for protection where it might be reasonably forthcoming.
propositions.quote: The onus is on the claimant to approach the state for protection in situations where state protection might be reasonably forthcoming.

propositions.text: The Board is guided by Supreme Court and Federal Court cases on state protection.
propositions.quote: The Board, in assessing the issue of state protection, is guided by a number of cases from the Supreme Court of Canada and the Federal Court.

paragraphs.summary: The court states legal principles on state protection and claimant's burden, guided by Supreme and Federal Court cases.

propositions.text: No government must guarantee perfect protection; effective control and serious efforts suffice to deny claim.
propositions.quote: No government is expected to guarantee perfect protection to all of its citizens at all times, and the fact that a state is not always successful in protecting its citizens, is not enough to justify a claim, especially where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police and civil authorities in place and is making serious efforts to protect its citizens.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that imperfect protection does not justify a claim if the state has effective control and makes serious efforts.

propositions.text: Local failures do not mean state fails unless part of broader pattern of inability or refusal to protect.
propositions.quote: Moreover, local failures by authorities to provide protection do not mean that the state on the whole fails to protect its citizens, unless those failures form part of a broader pattern of state inability or refusal to provide protection.

propositions.text: Claimants must approach other authorities if some police are corrupt.
propositions.quote: Indeed, if a claimant believes the actions of some police officers are corrupt, the onus is on the claimant to approach other members of the security forces or the authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The court states local failures do not prove state failure unless widespread; claimants must seek other authorities if police corrupt.

propositions.text: Claimant's burden to prove lack of state protection increases with state's democracy level.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the law states that the burden for the claimant to prove an absence of state protection is directly proportional to the level of democracy of that state.

propositions.text: More democratic states require claimants to exhaust all available courses of action.
propositions.quote: The more democratic the state's institutions, the greater the onus on the claimant to show he or she has exhausted all courses of action available.

propositions.text: Local failures do not mean state fails unless part of broader pattern of inability or refusal to protect.
propositions.quote: Moreover, local failures by the authorities to provide protection do not mean that the state as a whole fails to protect its citizens, unless the failures form part of a broader pattern of state inability or refusal to provide protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant's burden increases with democracy; local failures do not prove state failure unless widespread.

propositions.text: The test for state protection is adequacy, not perfect effectiveness.
propositions.quote: While the effectiveness of the protection is a relevant consideration, the preponderance of recent Federal court decisions has held that the test for a finding of state protection is whether the protection is adequate, rather than effective per se.

propositions.text: Claimants must show they took all reasonable steps to seek protection considering country context and interactions.
propositions.quote: A claimant must show that they have taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek protection, taking into account the context of the country of origin, the steps taken, and the claimant's interactions with the authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the test for state protection is adequacy; claimants must show reasonable steps to seek protection.

propositions.text: The Board must consider what steps the principal claimant took to seek state protection.
propositions.quote: The Board must consider what steps the principal claimant took to seek state protection.

propositions.text: Claimants fear skinheads and are visibly recognized as Romas; wife and children are less visible as Roma.
propositions.quote: The claimants fear "skinheads" and other individuals who hate Romas. According to the principal claimant, because they do not have blue eyes and blonde hair, they are visibly recognized as Romas. However, he acknowledged that since his wife originates from Poland, her visibility is not that of a Roma and his children as a consequence are "mixed."

paragraphs.summary: The court says it must consider claimant's steps to seek protection; claimant fears skinheads and is visibly Roma, wife and children less so.

propositions.text: The principal claimant and son testified about a 2005 incident involving police; claimant said no investigation, police said there was.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant and his son both testified with regard to the incident which occurred in XXXX 2005. The principal claimant testified that there was no investigation in this regard when a police officer himself was the perpetrator, whereas the foregoing paragraph indicates that there was, in fact, an investigation.

propositions.text: The claimant's son confirmed receiving a letter about the investigation and fine but lost the letter and did not follow up.
propositions.quote: At the second sitting, the claimant's son, XXXX, confirmed that he had received a letter indicating that there had been an investigation, he had to pay a fine, and the perpetrator was not located. XXXX was asked the whereabouts of this letter, to which he responded that it probably stayed in the house or was thrown out. He had not followed up on this letter, because according to him, he had lost his strength at this point.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant and son testified about a 2005 police incident; claimant said no investigation, son confirmed investigation and fine but lost letter.

propositions.text: The 2005 incident involved an unprovoked attack on the principal claimant by four young men and was reported to police.
propositions.quote: The XXXX 2005 incident, in which the principal claimant was approached by four young men and the victim of an unprovoked attack, was reported to the police.

propositions.text: The principal claimant tried to get a copy of the police report but was told it did not exist.
propositions.quote: according to the principal claimant although he attempted to obtain a copy of this report, he was told it did not exist.

paragraphs.summary: The 2005 attack on the principal claimant was reported to police, but he was told no report existed, per his claim.

propositions.text: In 2007, the principal claimant's wife left her job after a dispute involving an attack and theft accusation, choosing to resign.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2007, the principal claimant's wife decided to leave her place of employment after a dispute, in which she was attacked and accused of stealing money. She chose, at the recommendation of her husband, to resign.

propositions.text: She did not report the incident to police and said she did not go to police when asked why.
propositions.quote: However, she did not report the matter to the police. When asked why she did not, she responded "I did not go."

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's wife resigned after a 2007 dispute and did not report it to police, saying she did not go.

propositions.text: The 2008 incident was reported to police, who took photos; claimants submitted photos but acknowledged police took their own.
propositions.quote: The XXXX, 2008 incident, which according to the claimants was the pivotal point at which they decided to come to Canada, was reported to the police. Moreover, although the claimants submitted photographs of this incident, they acknowledged that the police themselves took photos.

propositions.text: The principal claimant was unaware of the investigation outcome and had not pursued it.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant was asked if he was aware of the outcome of any investigation in this regard. He was not aware and acknowledged that he had not pursued the matter.

paragraphs.summary: The 2008 incident was reported and photographed by police; the claimant was unaware of investigation results and did not pursue it.

propositions.text: Except for the 2005 incident, police pursued investigations but could not locate perpetrators; claimant did not pursue further.
propositions.quote: The Board concludes that with the exception of one incident, the XXXX 2005 incident, the police pursued investigation stemming from the reports. In the first instance, they were unable to locate the perpetrator and the principal claimant did not pursue the matter further.

paragraphs.summary: The Board finds police investigated all incidents except 2005, but perpetrators were not found and claimant did not pursue further.

propositions.text: The claimant's wife left her job voluntarily and chose not to report the matter to police.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant's wife chose to leave the restaurant of her own accord, and chose not to report the matter to the police.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's wife voluntarily left her job and did not report the incident to police, per the Board's finding.

propositions.text: The 2008 incident was reported and photographed by police, but claimants are unaware of investigation results.
propositions.quote: The incident, which according to the principal claimant, was the reason for the claimants' departure in 2008 was reported to the police, they took photographs, however the claimants are unaware of the results of this investigation.

paragraphs.summary: The Board finds the 2008 incident was reported and documented by police, but claimants do not know investigation outcomes.

propositions.text: Claimants have not provided clear and convincing evidence of state inability to protect them.
propositions.quote: In totality, the claimants have not provided clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect them.

paragraphs.summary: The Board concludes claimants failed to prove the state cannot protect them.

propositions.text: The Czech Republic is a multiparty parliamentary democracy with a bicameral parliament and about 10.2 million people.
propositions.quote: Documentary evidence indicates that the Czech Republic is a multiparty parliamentary democracy with a population of approximately 10.2 million. Legislative authority is vested in the bicameral parliament, consisting of a Chamber of Deputies and Senate.

paragraphs.summary: The Czech Republic is a multiparty democracy with a bicameral parliament and 10.2 million population.

propositions.text: National police enforce law and order; corruption remains a problem; Interior Ministry oversees police and investigates misconduct.
propositions.quote: The National police are responsible for enforcing the law and maintaining public order. While law enforcement bodies were generally effective, corruption remained a problem. The Interior Ministry oversees police actions and is responsible for investigating allegations of police misconduct.

paragraphs.summary: Police enforce law; corruption exists; Interior Ministry oversees police and investigates misconduct.

propositions.text: Laws provide right to fair trial; judiciary enforces it; defendants presumed innocent; trials are public.
propositions.quote: The laws provide for the right to a fair trial, and the independent judiciary generally enforced this right. Defendants enjoy a presumption of innocence and trials are public.

paragraphs.summary: The Czech legal system provides fair trials with presumption of innocence and public hearings.

propositions.text: Amnesty International reports Roma face discrimination in education, housing, health, employment, and racist attacks.
propositions.quote: According to Amnesty International, Roma continued to suffer discrimination from public officials and private individuals in education, housing, health and employment. Localities with marginalized Romani communities became targets of far-right groups; public officials continued to use racist language against the Roma.

paragraphs.summary: Amnesty International reports ongoing discrimination and racist attacks against Roma in multiple areas.

propositions.text: By law, police must respond to distress calls and notify complainants of outcomes; complainants have right to police report copies.
propositions.quote: However, by law, police must respond to all distress calls and notify parties of the outcome of their complaints. Every individual who files a complaint has the right to a copy of their police report.

propositions.text: Government points to Roma Police Assistants, Minority Liaison Officers, and Anti-Extremism Strategy as protection measures.
propositions.quote: When asked about police protection measures against discrimination and racially motivated violence, governmental interlocutors pointed to Roma Police Assistants, Minority Liaison Officers, and the Ministry of the Interior's Anti-Extremism Strategy.

propositions.text: The Ministry's 2008 Strategy on Policing Minorities includes training, minority employment, crime research, and maintaining RPA and MLO initiatives.
propositions.quote: In addition, the Ministry of the Interior's Strategy on Policing Minorities was passed on 9 April 2008 under government Resolution No. 384. The main objectives of this strategy include training on policing minority communities, efforts to employ minorities into the police force, researching crime in socially excluded localities, as well as maintaining the MLO and RPA initiatives.

paragraphs.summary: Police must respond to complaints and notify outcomes; government has programs and strategies to protect minorities including Roma.

propositions.text: Government and NGOs differ on police-Roma relations; police often arrive after conflicts resolved; Roma often refuse to cooperate.
propositions.quote: Governmental and NGO interlocutors varied in their assessment of police relations with Roma. However, e.g. in Brno, it was indicated that police are frequently called to the scene of a conflict only to be told that the situation has been resolved. Similarly, Diapa noted that Roma often refuse to cooperate in follow-up investigations to crimes they report, subsequently leading to cases being dropped.

propositions.text: Some NGOs and academics say police have negative, sometimes discriminatory attitudes toward Roma.
propositions.quote: However several NGO and academic interlocutors commented that the police generally have a negative view of Roma that sometimes includes discriminatory or disrespectful attitudes.

paragraphs.summary: Police-Roma relations vary; police often arrive late; Roma sometimes refuse cooperation; police attitudes can be discriminatory.

propositions.text: The Ombudsman investigates public sector mistreatment; no formal complaints against state police received since 2000.
propositions.quote: The Ombudsman seeks to investigate allegations of public sector mistreatment on the basis of a complaint or on his or her own initiative. The Ombudsman's office has jurisdiction covering a wide range of government ministries, as well as municipal and administrative authorities performing state functions. Since the first Ombudsman was appointed in 2000, he has received no formal complaints against the state police.

propositions.text: Ombudsman received unofficial NGO and individual reports of police bullying but could not act without formal complaints.
propositions.quote: However, he has received unofficial reports from NGOs and individuals alleging that they were bullied by state police, however, he could not act in the absence of formal complaints.

paragraphs.summary: The Ombudsman has received no formal police complaints but some unofficial bullying reports, unable to act without formal complaints.

propositions.text: NGOs actively provide services, monitor discrimination, bring cases to court, and oppose neo-Nazi groups for Roma.
propositions.quote: There are NGOs who are active and provide a range of services and activities for Roma. They monitor cases of private sector discrimination and bring such cases to court, provide legal assistance, monitor and speak out against neo-Nazi groups.

paragraphs.summary: NGOs provide services, monitor discrimination, litigate, and oppose neo-Nazi groups for Roma communities.

propositions.text: Several Brno-based NGOs provide social, legal, educational, and employment support services to Roma communities.
propositions.quote: DROM is a Brno-based NGO that carries out a wide range of activities in Romani communities, including social and legal services, child care, education and recreational activities. IQ Roma Servis is a Brno-based NGO that provides community and social field work, free counseling and legal services together with employment support for Roma clients in socially excluded localities. Other organizations include Socioklub, The Association of the Romanies in Moravia, Asvule Prava, the League of Human Rights etc.

paragraphs.summary: Brno NGOs provide social, legal, educational, and employment support to Roma communities.

propositions.text: The Roma Police Assistant program started in 2003, funded by government and municipalities, to assist Roma-police relations.
propositions.quote: The Roma Police Assistant (RPA) program was created in 2003 with seed money from the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MPSV). RPAs are now mainly funded by municipalities via National government grants.

propositions.text: RPAs help Roma victims file reports, educate on rights, assist investigations, and provide social services in excluded areas.
propositions.quote: RPA duties include establishing contact between Roma and the police, accompanying Romani victims of crime who wish to file a police report, educating victims on their legal rights and responsibilities, helping police investigate unreported crime, and assisting in the provision of social services in socially excluded localities.

propositions.text: No formal evaluations of RPAs exist, but police, municipalities, and NGOs view them as effective and improving trust.
propositions.quote: While no formal evaluations of their effectiveness have been carried out, police and municipalities believed RPAs to be efficient and valuable. Several NGO interlocutors also identified the existence of the RPA program as a sign of progress and two interlocutors claimed that RPAs have increased Romani trust in the police.

paragraphs.summary: The RPA program assists Roma-police relations and is viewed as effective and trust-building despite no formal evaluations.

propositions.text: No evidence shows Czech Republic is in complete breakdown; claimants must show all options exhausted; claimants failed to do so.
propositions.quote: There is nothing in the documentation before the Board to suggest that the Czech Republic is in a state of complete breakdown. The onus is on the claimant to show that he or she has exhausted all courses of action available. The claimants have not met that burden. They have not provided clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect them.

paragraphs.summary: The Board finds no evidence of state breakdown and that claimants failed to prove they exhausted all protection options.

propositions.text: Despite ongoing discrimination, Czech government makes serious efforts to protect Roma and assist inclusion.
propositions.quote: While acknowledging that discrimination against the Roma remains a problem, the preponderance of the documentary evidence indicates that the Czech Republic government is making very serious efforts to provide protection to the Roma whether as victims of hate crime, or assisting them in obtaining inclusion into Czech society.

paragraphs.summary: The Board finds the Czech government seriously tries to protect Roma and promote their inclusion despite discrimination.

propositions.text: No serious possibility of persecution or risk of harm exists for the principal claimant; claims are not in need of protection.
propositions.quote: For the foregoing reasons, the Board finds that there is not a serious possibility that the principal claimant would be subject to persecution, or that, on a balance of probabilities, his removal to the Czech Republic would subject him personally to a risk to his life, a risk of unusual treatment or punishment, or a danger of torture. Since all claims are based on the fears of the principal claimant, they are also found not to be in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The Board concludes the principal claimant faces no serious risk of persecution or harm and does not need protection.

propositions.text: All claims are rejected.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, all claims are rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes all claims are rejected.
